title: Solid, liquid, gas
_map: Solid, liquid, gas (stretch, usually Y4). Big idea: materials change state when heated or cooled. Creative: melt ice blocks into water, then into steam; what happens when it cools?
_story: Steve's ice block in the drinking trough is melting. It heats some in a pan and it disappears into steam. Where did the water go? Ismaeel follows it through three states.
_stepChain: temperature (hot-and-cold) → ice is solid: keeps its shape → warm it: it melts into water, a liquid: flows → heat more: it boils into steam, a gas: spreads out → these are called states → cool steam: water drops again (lid) → Steve thinks the water vanished

talk.ask: What are the three states of water?
talk.goodAnswer: solid ice, liquid water, and gas: steam.

talk.ask: Where does the water go when it boils?
talk.goodAnswer: it turns into steam, a gas, which spreads out into the air.

handsOn: Put an ice cube on a plate and watch it melt. With a grown-up, hold a cold spoon over a steaming cup: tiny water drops appear!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I've got a block of ice from the frozen pond. It's hard and keeps its shape. What happens if I warm it up?
Ice is a solid. Solids keep their shape: you can hold them, and they don't spread out.
Warm it up, and the ice melts into water. Water is a liquid. Liquids flow, and take the shape of whatever they're in.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Now I'll heat it much more. Oh! The water is disappearing. It's gone forever!

question.onRight: Yes. It turns into steam, a gas, and spreads out into the air.

0.hint: Look above the pan. What's rising up?
0.say: It hasn't vanished. The water turns into steam, a gas, and spreads out into the air. You can't always see it, but it's there.

2.mistake: thinks the pan soaks it up
2.hint: Metal pans don't soak things up. Look at what's rising.
2.say: The pan doesn't soak it up. The water turns into steam, a gas, which rises and spreads into the air.

question.reveal: Water boils into steam, a gas. Gases spread out to fill the space.

narration.text: Solid, liquid and gas are called the three states. Water can be all three: ice, water and steam. When steam cools on a cold lid, it turns back into water drops. It was there all along!

rule.text: Heat it: solid → liquid → gas. Cool it: back again.
rule.ask: Can you say the three states of water? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Ice is solid, water is liquid, and steam is a gas. Heating changes it one way, and cooling changes it back.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: chocolate melts in your hand. Is melted chocolate a solid or a liquid?
bonus.reveal: A liquid! Put it in the fridge, and it turns back into a solid.
